newsitem.title: USA: Boeing sending engineer to Ecuador crash site.
newsitem.headline: Boeing sending engineer to Ecuador crash site.

text.p: Officials from Boeing Co., engine maker Pratt & Whitney and the U.S. National Transportation Safety Board will help determine why a Millon Air 707 cargo plane crashed in Ecuador, a Boeing spokesman said Wednesday.
They will go to the crash site in the coastal city of Manta, spokesman Dick Schleh said.

At least 22 people were killed and 60 injured, most on the ground, when the Miami-bound jet carrying flowers and frozen fish ploughed into a densely populated poor neighbourhood shortly after takeoff late Tuesday.
Schleh said it was too early to speculate about a cause.

He said the Millon Air 707-320C originally was delivered to American Airlines in 1967 and later converted to cargo use. It had about 65,000 hours of flight time, which he said was "not particularly high" for a plane that age.

The 707 was world's first commercial jetliner when it was initially delivered in 1958. More than 1,000 were delivered to civilian and military customers, and about 380 are still being flown, mostly by government agencies. Boeing stopped producing the plane commercially in 1978.
